sources_considered.why: Primary field research reports practical benefits over a six-month experiment. The returned text bears an August 24, 2026 date, which is used conservatively for availability.
Read to identify the paper, authors, experimental scope, and version history.
A dated company release documents useful local-model functionality and offline operation.
Readable, but the current documentation lacks sufficiently clear publication provenance; the dated announcement was preferred.

evidence_items.publisher: Eleanor Wiske Dillon, Sonia Jaffe, Nicole Immorlica, and Christopher T. Stanton; arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Introduction, discussion of application use; experiment dates described earlier in the introduction
evidence_items.explanation: The six-month workplace experiment, conducted across firms between September 2023 and October 2024, reports sustained practical use and time savings. This meets a practical-usefulness reading of the antecedent, without proving lasting economy-wide value.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'OpenAI-like Structured Output API'; offline operation described in the introduction
evidence_items.explanation: The release supports structured outputs, document interaction, and local serving in an application described as operating offline. This weakens the premise that useful LLM applications necessarily incur cloud-inference payments, but does not supply a complete payment audit or settle future consolidation.

unresolved_gaps: No deadline determines when universal payments must begin.
No comprehensive contracts or payment dataset establishes a cut from every LLM application.
Local operation does not by itself establish the absence of all relevant licensing payments.
No decisive event settles the eventual universal-payment prediction.
